$comment: IGNORED BY THE LOADER. The Ikarus 'liquid glass' component set. These are OURS: the source is in this repository, the licence is this repository's licence (Apache-2.0), and their provenance is a path rather than a URL to somebody else's server. A Daedalus-built GUI should reach for these FIRST -- they exist, they work, and their licence is not in question. Props below were read from the .tsx definition sites on 2026-07-29, not inferred.

entries.name: glass/GlassPanel
entries.title: GlassPanel
entries.purpose: The base liquid-glass surface: backdrop blur and saturate, a 1px light edge, and an iridescent diffraction ring. Use it as the outermost container of any panel, shell region, or floating surface that should read as frosted glass. Reveal-on-mount is OFF by default because a panel that is part of the shell has always been there.

provenance.note: Props read from the definition site, not inferred.

props.name: reveal
props.description: Animate the surface in on mount. Turn on only for a surface that genuinely just came into existence.

props.name: revealDistance
props.description: Travel distance for the reveal in px. Defaults to the nudge token (6).

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Spread onto the underlying div.

props.name: children
props.description: Panel content.

entries.notes: Wraps the .glass class from styles.css. Without `reveal` it renders a plain div and pulls in no motion runtime at render time.

entries.name: glass/GlassCard
entries.title: GlassCard
entries.purpose: A lighter, thinner glass tile for content nested inside a GlassPanel. Use it for a repeated item in a list or grid -- a queued task, a drafted network, a metric tile. Reveal-on-mount is ON by default because a card's arrival IS the state change it reports.

props.name: hoverable
props.description: Adds the hover lift (whileHover, 1px, the hairline token).

props.name: reveal
props.description: Animate in on mount.

entries.notes: Reveal travels 6px (nudge) rather than 12px (rise), so a card arriving inside a bubble reads as depth rather than as a competing animation. Declares exit="hidden", inert until an <AnimatePresence> sits above it.

entries.name: glass/GlassButton
entries.title: GlassButton
entries.purpose: A glass pill button. `primary` paints the accent-gradient variant. Use it for any click target that is not a dock icon or a composer send button. Defaults type="button", so it will not accidentally submit a form.

props.name: primary
props.description: Paint the accent-gradient variant.

entries.notes: The one glass primitive with NO framer-motion import: its press and hover feedback stay in CSS, where a pseudo-class already expresses the state.

entries.name: glass/GlassSheet
entries.title: GlassSheet
entries.purpose: A full glass overlay that slides up over the main content, with a scrim and a titled header carrying a back button. Use it for a heavy secondary view -- a graph, a code map, a settings surface -- that should cover the primary view without navigating away from it.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the sheet is showing.

props.name: title
props.description: Header title.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called by the back button and by a scrim click.

props.name: children
props.description: Sheet body.

entries.usage:
<GlassSheet open={view === 'graph'} title="Code map" subtitle="1,284 modules" onClose={() => setView('chat')}>
  <GraphCanvas />
</GlassSheet>
entries.notes: Stays MOUNTED when closed and is deliberately not wrapped in AnimatePresence, because its children are heavy views whose state must survive a close. Sets role="dialog", aria-modal and aria-hidden. It does NOT trap focus -- add that if you use it for a true modal.

entries.name: glass/SegmentedControl
entries.title: SegmentedControl
entries.purpose: An iOS-style segmented control for choosing exactly one option from a short, fixed set. Use it instead of tabs when the options are peers and the set is small enough to show at once. The selection is one element that travels between segments rather than two that cross-fade.

props.name: options
props.description: The segments, in display order.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected option. Undefined renders with no active segment.

entries.notes: The thumb carries a layoutId scoped per control instance via useId, so two controls on one screen cannot claim the same shared-layout identity. Under reduced motion the layoutId is dropped entirely and the thumb cross-fades.

entries.name: glass/Dock
entries.title: Dock
entries.purpose: The 64px vertical icon rail pinned to the far left of the shell. It is the app's primary navigation. Fill it with DockGroup sections, DockItem buttons and DockSpacer gaps. It reveals its items in sequence on first mount -- the one place in the app where a staggered entrance is honest.
entries.usage:
<Dock>
  <DockGroup>
    <DockItem icon={<Home size={18} />} label="Chat" active onClick={() => go('chat')} />
  </DockGroup>
  <DockSpacer />
  <DockGroup>
    <DockItem icon={<Settings size={18} />} label="Theme" />
  </DockGroup>
</Dock>
entries.notes: Renders a <nav>. Also exports DockGroup (one travelling highlight per group) and DockSpacer (a flex gap). The stagger tightens as items are added so the whole reveal never runs past 240ms.

entries.name: glass/DockItem
entries.title: DockItem
entries.purpose: One button in the Dock: an icon, a tooltip label, an optional unread badge, and an active state. The active surface is a real element that slides from the old button to the new one, so switching views reads as the highlight moving rather than repainting.

props.name: label
props.description: Used as title, aria-label and the hover tooltip.

props.name: badge
props.description: Show the unread dot.

entries.usage: <DockItem icon={<Home size={18} />} label="Chat" active badge onClick={go} />
entries.notes: Must be rendered inside a DockGroup to get a group-scoped travelling pill; outside one it falls back to a shared 'root' id. The motion pill owns background, border-color and box-shadow on .dockbtn.active -- decorate through a pseudo-element instead of those three.

entries.name: glass/LiveRail
entries.title: LiveRail
entries.purpose: The collapsible right-hand column of live monitoring cards. Use it for at-a-glance status that updates on its own -- token spend, running jobs, host health. Fill it with RailCard children; it reveals them in sequence on mount and tightens the offset so the column is settled inside 240ms however many cards it carries.
entries.notes: Renders an <aside>. The COLLAPSE is deliberately not animated here: the shell collapses the rail by switching a grid track to 0 with display:none, which cannot be transitioned. Animating it needs a prop from the view layer.

entries.name: glass/RailCard
entries.title: RailCard
entries.purpose: One titled card inside a LiveRail: a header row with an optional leading icon and an optional trailing badge, plus a body. Use it for a single live metric or a short status list.

props.name: icon
props.description: Rendered before the title.

props.name: badge
props.description: Rendered at the right end of the header row.

entries.usage:
<RailCard title="Hosts" icon={<Server size={13} />} badge={<LiveDot status="good" />}>
  2 of 2 reachable
</RailCard>

entries.name: glass/LiveDot
entries.title: LiveDot
entries.purpose: A small breathing status dot: good, warn or bad. Use it anywhere a single health or liveness state needs to be visible without words -- beside a host name, in a rail card header, next to a running job.
entries.notes: Imports motion.css but NONE of the motion runtime: the pulse is an ambient CSS @keyframes with no React state behind it. motion.css replaces the shipped box-shadow-spread keyframe with a transform-and-opacity pseudo-element, so a screen full of dots costs the main thread nothing per frame.

entries.name: glass/ChatBubble
entries.title: ChatBubble
entries.purpose: One transcript bubble in a two-voice conversation: 'ik' renders on the left with a Sparkles avatar, 'me' on the right with a letter. Each side arrives from its own edge so the transcript reads as two voices rather than one feed. Use it for any chat, log, or agent transcript.

props.name: role
props.description: 'ik' = the assistant (left), 'me' = the user (right).

props.name: avatar
props.description: Overrides the default avatar.

props.name: children
props.description: Message body.

entries.usage:
<ChatBubble role="ik">Ready. What are we building?</ChatBubble>
<ChatBubble role="me">A dashboard.</ChatBubble>
entries.notes: Declares exit="hidden", which is inert until the message list is wrapped in <AnimatePresence> -- that wrap is the only change needed to animate removals, no prop and no API. Deliberately does NOT use `layout`: shared-layout projection inside a container that auto-scrolls to the bottom is a known way to make the two fight.

entries.name: glass/Composer
entries.title: Composer
entries.purpose: The chat input: optional suggestion chips, an auto-growing textarea capped at 120px, and a send button that visibly arms as the field fills. Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a newline. Use it as the bottom bar of any chat surface.

props.name: chips
props.description: Suggestion chips shown above the field.

props.name: onChip
props.description: Defaults to onChange(chip) when omitted.

props.name: busy
props.description: Disables send and suppresses the Enter shortcut.

props.name: extra
props.description: Slot rendered above the input, e.g. an inline confirm row.

entries.usage:
<Composer
  value={draft}
  onChange={setDraft}
  onSend={send}
  chips={['Explain this', 'Write a test']}
  busy={pending}
/>
entries.notes: All three motion pieces sit in the acknowledgement tier (140ms, no spring) because all three are feedback about the user's input. Height is auto-grown by writing style.height once per keystroke and is deliberately NOT animated -- interpolating it would put a layout pass on the compositor's critical path.

entries.name: motion/tokens
entries.title: Ikarus motion vocabulary
entries.purpose: The only place a duration, easing, spring, travel distance, scale or stagger may be written down. Two tiers: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT (<=180ms, no spring, feedback about the input) and STATE CHANGE (220-360ms, spatial, spring, feedback about the system). Read this before animating anything, and take numbers from it rather than inventing them.

props.name: DURATION_MS
props.type: { instant: 90, ack: 140, move: 240, exit: 220, enter: 320, ambient: 420 }
props.description: Milliseconds are the source of truth because that is the unit the CSS half speaks.

props.name: EASE
props.description: glass = [.32,.72,0,1], the house curve.

props.name: SPRING
props.description: Both damped to within a percent of critical: an instrument settles, it does not bounce.

props.name: staggerFor
props.description: Per-child offset that keeps a whole list reveal under totalCap.

props.name: COMPOSITED_PROPS
props.description: The only properties that may be animated.

props.name: LAYOUT_TRIGGERING_PROPS
props.description: Banned outright. motion.spec.ts audits every variant factory against this list.

entries.usage:
import { DURATION_MS, EASE, DISTANCE } from '../../motion';

const transition = { duration: DURATION_MS.ack / 1000, ease: EASE.ack };
entries.notes: The tier boundary is ASSERTED by motion.spec.ts (ack <= 180ms, state >= 200ms) and useMotion.ts warns if the CSS custom properties and these constants ever drift. Both are guards, not documentation.

entries.name: motion/useReducedMotionPref
entries.title: useReducedMotionPref
entries.purpose: Reads the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting so a component can drop travel and scale while keeping the opacity change. Every motion-driven glass primitive calls it. Use it whenever you write a variant by hand: a state change must still be VISIBLE under reduced motion, it just must not move.

props.name: returns
props.description: True when the user has asked for reduced motion.

entries.usage:
const reduced = useReducedMotionPref();
const variants = useMemo(() => revealVariants(reduced), [reduced]);
